---
title: "Modules, Cargo, and Tests"
description: "One Rust language concept taught with one short runnable example and a precise explanation."
---

## The question

**How do you organise code without building a large framework?**

A module defines a namespace and visibility boundary. Cargo builds and tests crates. Most basic demonstrations need only one file; a procedural macro is the exception because the compiler requires a special crate type.

## The rule to remember

Keep examples small and test ordinary functions before extracting many packages.

## The smallest complete example

Paste into `main.rs` and run with `rustc --edition 2024 main.rs && ./main`. The [Rust examples page](examples/index.qmd) describes how to check all snippets automatically.

~~~rust
mod math {
    pub fn double(n: i32) -> i32 { n * 2 }
}
fn main() {
    println!("{}", math::double(3)); // 6
}
~~~

**Follow the state:** `mod math` creates a namespace and `pub` makes `double` accessible from its parent. Without `pub`, calling it from `main` would violate Rust visibility rules.

## Important limitation

Run with `rustc --edition 2024 main.rs`. For a Cargo project, `cargo test` discovers `#[test]` functions. Rust 2024 edition affects language defaults; it does not require learning every new edition feature before understanding modules.
